messages:
maria: Quick follow-up to the onboarding RFC — we need to finalize the "dead-letter" / failure-contract behavior for model admissions. asking for tradeoffs before I write the short RFC addendum.

maria: Proposed defaults: 1) transient failures: retry window + ephemeral artifacts (24h), 2) deterministic validation failures: persist artifact bundle + compact diff + TTL 30d, 3) catastrophic binary mismatch (checksum / incompatible tokenizer): quarantine longer (90d) and require manual sign-off. Thoughts? :thinking_face: 

tom: +1 on categories. we should be explicit about what we keep in the persisted bundle vs pointers. saving big compiled binaries for 30d is expensive. prefer artifact pointers + minimum repro inputs and metadata.

sree: Agree on pointers. Also add a small reproducible runner (docker-lite) that can be spawned from the bundle to re-run the failing check without pulling full GC artifacts. that helps root-cause without long-term storage.

alex: Can we quantify cost hit? If we only store pointers + minimal repro (prompt + tokenized ids + seed + config) we can reduce storage 90% vs full binary. But operationally we need to ensure the pointers are stable across model registries. i.e. the pointer must be to an immutable object (s3 version id or dedup key).

maria: yep — requirement: pointers reference immutable storage with object version. otherwise the dead-letter becomes meaningless. add a checksum field in the metadata so we can detect pointer drift.

jen: about telemetry: what signals do we route to the dead-letter vs to monitoring? e.g., golden_input_mismatch should generate an alert and create a persisted bundle. transient GPU OOM should be retried and only go DL after N retries. recommend:
- metric-classify: "regression" vs "transient" vs "invariant-break"
- regression (perf p99 increase > 2x OR token-error-rate increase > 1%) -> persisted bundle + alert
- transient (OOM, infra hickup) -> ephemeral + retry 3x
- invariant-break (tokenizer mismatch, checksum) -> quarantine + manual workflow

sam: also ensure the retry policy is configurable per org. enterprise customers may want longer retry windows or different thresholds. defaults are fine but expose knob in the intake descriptor.

maria: good point. we'll expose retry_window_seconds, max_retries, and deadletter_policy.ref (enum: keep_pointers, persist_binaries, quarantine). default: keep_pointers.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of onboarding-worker v2 scheduled tonight 23:00 UTC — will include the new DL metadata fields. Rolling update to 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

tom: note on compatibility checks: we need a small shim that runs model binary through a tokenizer-compatibility test (tokenization hash + roundtrip) and also an embedding-stability check for a few golden inputs. if either fails -> invariant-break. keep that shim deterministic and small.

sree: about the bench integration: lightweight bench (quick perf probe) should run pre-admit. deep bench runs async post-admit on Dedicated and Private customers. if lightweight bench flags a 20% perf regression we should hold admit until human review. do we want automatic fallback to a lower-capacity runtime?

alex: automatic fallback is risky for customer-facing model registry. prefer: auto-flag + canary-tagging. admit but tag model as "canary: degraded" and route production traffic only after opt-in. Automation can later enable fallback routes but require explicit opt-in.

maria: summary of decisions so far (will add to RFC addendum):
- three failure classes (transient, regression, invariant-break) with default handling policies.
- persistent bundle = pointers + minimal repro + metadata + checksums; full binaries persisted only if policy= persist_binaries.
- small docker-lite repro runner included in bundle for fast local reruns.
- telemetry thresholds for automatic classification; make knobs configurable per-org.
- lightweight bench = gate; deep bench = post-admit async.
- default behavior: keep_pointers, retry 3x, ephemeral artifacts 24h, persist bundles 30d, quarantine 90d.

jen: can we add a required metadata field: "failing_signal" (string), "top_metric_delta" (string or numeric) + stacktrace-ish free text? helps triage.

maria: yes — plan to add failing_signal, metric_delta, repro_prompt_id, pointer_list, checksum, runner_image_tag, assigned_oncall (optional).

sam: action items:
- maria: draft RFC addendum with above defaults and sample JSON examples for DL bundles (due EOD tomorrow)
- tom + sree: prototype docker-lite runner and tokenizer-shim (PR by next Tues)
- alex: produce cost estimate for pointer-only vs persist-binaries (numbers by Friday)
- jen: write telemetry spec for classification thresholds and monitoring alerts (next Wed)

alex: nit — include a small example blob in the RFC that shows minimal repro format, e.g.:
```{
  "repro_prompt": "Translate to French: Hello world",
  "token_ids": [154, 23, 4],
  "seed": 42,
  "model_config": "quantized-int8-v2",
  "checksum": "sha256:abcd...",
  "pointer": "s3://models/registry/123456:v2"
}```

maria: perfect. i'll include that and also a sample lifecycle diagram (ingest -> lightweight bench -> admit/canary -> deep bench -> GA).

jen: one more UX ask — surfacing DL state in the Console with a short triage button ("replay locally") that triggers the docker-lite runner. the button should include the repro bundle pointer and auto-open a run log. small design ticket pls.

maria: noted — i'll open a Console ticket and link it in the addendum.

tom: last thought — long-term refactor note: the intake descriptor is getting crowded. propose v2: split acceptance_policy (deadletter, retries, thresholds) from runtime_profile (batching, kv-cache hints). land the DL work as a backwards-compatible extension, then do descriptor split in next quarter.

sree: agreed. keep backwards compatibility. maybe add a schema version field on descriptor.

maria: thanks everyone. i'll write up the addendum and ping for a quick review. tagging @tom @sree @alex @jen @sam. :rocket:
